South Derbyshire's population increased by around 12,600 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population passed 100,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of South Derbyshire increased by 13.3%, from just over 94,600 in 2011 to around 107,200 in 2021.

The population here increased by a greater percentage than the overall population of the East Midlands (7.7%), and by a greater percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, South Derbyshire was home to around 2.3 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 2.0 in 2011. This area was among the lowest 35% for population density across English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was higher in South Derbyshire than across the East Midlands

An older South Derbyshire

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of South Derbyshire increased by two years, from 40 to 42 years of age.

This area had a slightly higher average (median) age than the East Midlands as a whole in 2021 (41 years) and a higher average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 50 to 64 years rose by around 4,100 (an increase of 22.5%), while the number of residents between 35 and 49 years fell by just under 1,200 (5.3% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 50 and 64 years increased by 1.6 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Fewer adults working long hours

South Derbyshire saw the East Midlands' third-largest percentage-point fall in the proportion of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked over 49 hours per week (from 15.0% in 2011 to 12.0% in 2021).

Across the region, only Derbyshire Dales (from 18.3% to 15.1%) and Harborough (from 16.5% to 13.3%) saw a greater decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked over 49 hours per week.

Every local authority area across the East Midlands saw a fall in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked over 49 hours per week, as the regional percentage fell from 12.9% to 10.6%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults in employment who worked 49 hours or more in South Derbyshire decreased by 2.9 percentage points

Rise in private renting

The increase in the percentage of privately-rented homes was greater across the East Midlands (3.8 percentage points) than in South Derbyshire (1.6 percentage points).

In South Derbyshire, the percentage of private renting increased from 13.0% in 2011 to 14.7% in 2021. During the same period, the regional percentage increased from 14.9% to 18.7%.

The rate of social renting in South Derbyshire remained at 9.9%, while the rate of home ownership decreased from 75.4% to 74.5%.

Private renting in South Derbyshire increased by 1.6 percentage points

Disability in South Derbyshire

In 2021, 7.0% of South Derbyshire residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 9.1% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot was greater in South Derbyshire (2.1 percentage points) than across the East Midlands (1.6 percentage points, from 9.3% to 7.7%). Across England, the proportion fell by 1.6 percentage points, from 9.1% to 7.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in South Derbyshire decreased by 2.1 percentage points

Unpaid care in South Derbyshire

In 2021, 4.7% of South Derbyshire residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 7.8% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just under 1 in 50 people (1.8%) reported providing between 20 and 49 hours of unpaid care each week, compared with 1.5% in 2011. The proportion of South Derbyshire residents (aged five years and over) that provided at least 50 hours of weekly unpaid care increased from 2.6% to 2.7%.

The decrease in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care was greater in South Derbyshire (3.1 percentage points) than across the East Midlands (2.8 percentage points, from 7.4% to 4.6%). Across England, the proportion fell by 2.8 percentage points, from 7.2% to 4.4%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in South Derbyshire decreased by 3.1 percentage points

Religion in South Derbyshire

In 2021, 43.0% of South Derbyshire residents reported having "No religion", up from 26.8% in 2011. The rise of 16.3 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in South Derbyshire. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the East Midlands, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 27.5% to 40.0%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 47.4% of people in South Derbyshire described themselves as Christian (down from 64.0%), while 5.5% did not state their religion (down from 6.6% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

South Derbyshire residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 98,500 South Derbyshire residents said they were born in England. This represented 91.9% of the local population. The figure has risen from around 88,600 in 2011, which at the time represented 93.6% of South Derbyshire's population.

Scotland was the next most represented, with just over 1,200 South Derbyshire residents reporting this country of birth (1.2%). This figure was down from just over 1,300 in 2011, which at the time represented 1.4% of the population of South Derbyshire.

The number of South Derbyshire residents born in India rose from around 700 in 2011 (0.7% of the local population) to just under 1,200 in 2021 (1.1%).

In 2021, 91.9% of South Derbyshire residents reported their country of birth as England

People looking after their family or home in South Derbyshire

In 2021, 3.8% of South Derbyshire residents (aged 16 years and over) said they were economically inactive because they were looking after their family or home. This figure was at a similar level in 2011 (3.7%).

The percentage of people who were economically inactive because they were looking after their family or home increased from 3.6% to 4.3% across the East Midlands. Across England, the percentage increased from 4.0% to 4.8%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were looking after their family or home (economically inactive) in South Derbyshire increased by 0.2 percentage points

Health in South Derbyshire

In 2021, 47.6% of South Derbyshire residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 45.4% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 34.8% to 34.7%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of South Derbyshire residents describing their health as "very bad" was 1.0% (similar to 2011), while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 4.3% to 3.7%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in very bad health in South Derbyshire decreased by 0.2 percentage points

National identity in South Derbyshire

In 2021, 3.2% of South Derbyshire residents did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK. This figure increased from 1.9% in 2011.

In 2021, 0.8% of residents identified with a UK and non-UK national identity, compared with 0.4% in 2011. The percentage of residents in South Derbyshire that identified as "British only" increased from 13.8% to 56.4%.

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK was greater across the East Midlands (2.7 percentage points, from 5.8% to 8.5%) than in South Derbyshire (1.3 percentage points). Across England, the percentage increased by 1.7 percentage points, from 8.2% to 10.0%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in South Derbyshire increased by 1.3 percentage points

Family in South Derbyshire

Of South Derbyshire households, 21.2% included a couple but no children in 2021, down from 22.4% in 2011.

In 2021, just over one in five households (21.1%) included a couple with dependent children, compared with 23.1% in 2011. The percentage of single family households including a couple living with only non-dependent children remained at 6.8%.

This area had the region’s joint highest percentage of households including a couple but no children (alongside North Kesteven). East Lindsey had the East Midlands' next highest percentage of households including a couple but no children (20.7%), while Leicester had the region's lowest percentage (11.7%).

The percentage of households including a couple without children in South Derbyshire decreased by 1.1 percentage points

More adults never married or in a civil partnership

Of South Derbyshire residents aged 16 years and over, 32.8% said they had never been married or in a civil partnership in 2021, up from 28.7% in 2011.

In 2021, just under one in two people (49.2%) said they were married or in a registered civil partnership, compared with 52.9% in 2011. The percentage of adults in South Derbyshire that had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership increased from 9.4% to 9.6%.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership was greater in South Derbyshire (4.2 percentage points) than across the East Midlands (3.8 percentage points, from 32.3% to 36.1%). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.3 percentage points, from 34.6% to 37.9%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in South Derbyshire increased by 4.2 percentage points

Ethnic groups in South Derbyshire

In 2021, 3.6% of South Derbyshire residents identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category, up from 2.5% in 2011. The 1.1 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the East Midlands, the percentage of people from the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" ethnic group increased from 6.5% to 8.0%, while across England the percentage increased from 7.8% to 9.6%.

In 2021, 93.1% of people in South Derbyshire identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 95.7% in 2011), while 1.8% identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category (compared with 1.1% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Black, Black British, Black Welsh, Caribbean or African" category increased from 0.4% in 2011 to 0.8% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.
